clue.text: What shows the way to autograph mail

parts.note: to autograph something is to sign it
post is the British word for mail

explanation.surface: Someone asks how to get their autographed letter sent off.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside marker with arms pointing towards destinations guides travellers, so it shows the way.

clue.text: Celebration is quiet in a lot of lodgings

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the end is dropped

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
taken as written
digs is British slang for rented lodgings

explanation.surface: A party is kept quiet in a crowded boarding house.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindig is a lively party or festive gathering.

clue.text: Rise in fancy costume

definitions.meaning: first meaning, a verb: to rise from bed or a seat
second meaning, a noun: an elaborate outfit

explanation.surface: Someone stands up wearing fancy dress.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb is two words; the noun is usually written as one or hyphenated.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the verb for leaving bed and also a noun for an odd outfit.

clue.text: What can be scored with Scrabble tile directly

parts.note: points are what players score
the blank is the letterless Scrabble tile

explanation.surface: A player scores straight away with a Scrabble tile.
explanation.definitionFit: Point-blank as an adverb means bluntly and straight out, as in refusing outright.

clue.text: Saint and vampire slayer not keeping bishop close

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for saint

indicators.note: not keeping something means it is let go and removed

parts.note: Buffy the Vampire Slayer is the TV heroine
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A saint and a vampire hunter refuse to keep a bishop nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' is the adjective for airless weather, not the verb or 'near'.
explanation.definitionFit: Close weather is humid and airless, just as a stuffy room lacks fresh air.

clue.text: Finished port after daughter's gone

indicators.note: once the daughter has gone, her abbreviation is removed from the word

parts.note: Dover is the English Channel ferry port
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A trip to a harbour town is over once the daughter has left.
explanation.walkthrough: Dover is the Kent port facing France; dropping its D leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is over has come to an end, a synonym for finished.

clue.text: Pay no heed to stringed instrument note

parts.note: the viola is a stringed instrument
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A musician ignores the note played on a stringed instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: To violate a rule or law is to disregard or break it.

clue.text: Anger about new compass

indicators.note: about means going round, enclosing the next part

parts.note: rage is anger
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone is furious about a newly bought compass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anger' tempts an anagram of its own letters, but it is a synonym wrapping a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Compass in the sense of scope or extent means the full span something covers.

clue.text: Take part in conspiracy, rueing it badly

indicators.note: doing something badly suggests the letters come out in a muddled arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A plotter joins a conspiracy and soon regrets it bitterly.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to intrigue is to plot secretly with others, joining a scheme.

clue.text: Second working satellite

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second, as in 'just a mo'
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A backup orbiting satellite has come into service.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth's natural satellite is the body that orbits it each month.

clue.text: Teams get confused on horseback somehow

parts.note: sides are teams
to addle is to muddle or become confused

explanation.surface: Teams get muddled while riding horses.
explanation.walkthrough: The last word looks like an anagram signal, but it belongs to the definition: the answer is one particular way of sitting on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding with both legs on one side of the mount is a specific manner of being mounted.

clue.text: Party time outside record store

indicators.note: one part sits outside, wrapping round the other

parts.note: a do is a party
T is the abbreviation for time
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: It is party time at a shop selling records.
explanation.walkthrough: The joined pair goes round the record, which sits after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a warehouse or storehouse where goods are kept.

clue.text: Warship's tackle kept by chance

indicators.note: something kept by another is held inside it

parts.note: fate is chance or destiny
rig is a ship's tackle, its ropes and gear

explanation.surface: A naval vessel's gear has survived by sheer luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A frigate is a type of fast naval vessel, so it is a kind of warship.

clue.text: Flock of geese get going initially in high wind

indicators.note: those letters are placed inside the following word

parts.note: a gale is a high wind

indicators.note: initially means taking only the opening letters of the words before it

parts.note: first letter of get
first letter of going

explanation.surface: Geese take off as a strong wind gets up.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaggle is the collective noun for a group of geese on the ground.

clue.text: Ship's volume filled with energy

indicators.note: something filled with another holds it inside

parts.note: a gallon is a measure of volume
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A vessel's capacity is full of power.
explanation.definitionFit: A galleon was a large old Spanish sailing ship.

clue.text: Begrudge what one pays for housing round southeast

indicators.note: one word goes round, enclosing the other

parts.note: rent is the regular payment for a home
SE is the compass abbreviation for southeast

explanation.surface: A tenant grudges paying for a home in the southeast of England.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent something is to feel bitter about it, to begrudge it.

clue.text: Little fish holds nothing for one tiny child

indicators.note: holding one thing for another means a swap, the first taking the place of the second

parts.note: a tiddler is a small fish
O is zero, nothing
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A small fish is keeping nothing for one little child.
explanation.walkthrough: In the fish's name the letter for one is replaced by the letter for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A toddler is a very young child just learning to walk.

clue.text: Chaps grow old in household

parts.note: chaps are men
to age is to grow old

explanation.surface: Men get older living at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A ménage, from French, is a domestic establishment, the members of a home.

clue.text: Outstanding amount of emotional stability

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the sum still owed on an account
second meaning: a steady, even state of mind

explanation.surface: Someone has a great deal of emotional steadiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' looks like praise but means unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the remaining sum owed on an account and a steady mental equilibrium.

clue.text: Particular type of note and unit of currency

parts.note: B is a musical note
the rand is South Africa's currency

explanation.surface: A certain kind of banknote and a monetary unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' suggests a banknote beside currency, but it is a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand is a make of product, so a particular kind or variety.

clue.text: Present conflict welcomed by a Democrat

indicators.note: a guest welcomed by hosts is taken in among them

parts.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for a Democrat
war is armed conflict

explanation.surface: A war-themed gift is gladly received by a Democratic politician.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is a prize presented to someone, so it is a present in the noun sense.

clue.text: Shakespearean character I found in Lear possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare role is discovered within King Lear.
explanation.walkthrough: Lear is a Shakespeare king, but this character is the spirit from The Tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariel is the airy spirit who serves Prospero in The Tempest.

clue.text: Top copy with supplement of Times

parts.note: to ape is to copy or mimic
x is the multiplication sign, read as 'times'

explanation.surface: The best copy of the newspaper comes with its magazine supplement.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times capitalised suggests the newspaper, but it is the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the highest point or peak of something, its top.

clue.text: Bring down charge for burial of rubbish

parts.note: to land an aircraft is to bring it down
to charge a glass is to fill it

explanation.surface: A council lowers its fee for disposing of household waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Landfill is the disposal of waste by burying it in the ground at a tip.

clue.text: Sci-fi film expected around November

indicators.note: one word goes around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: something due is expected
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A science-fiction movie is due out in November.
explanation.definitionFit: The desert-planet epic from Frank Herbert's novel has been filmed several times, the latest by Villeneuve.

clue.text: Craftsman thriving in barrack

indicators.note: one word sits inside the other

parts.note: to barrack is to jeer at a speaker
someone doing well is thriving

explanation.surface: An artisan does well living in army quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barrack' looks like a soldier's building, but it is the verb for heckling.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeweller is a skilled maker of rings and necklaces, a craft worker.
